question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $8,$ denoted ${3}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
3\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(3,8)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $8.$

Since the modulus $n=8$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $3$ (modulo $8$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2} & ≡3\cdot 3≡9≡1\cdot 8+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $3\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,8).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $3$ modulo $8$ is $3.$
